newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Undercover soldiers shock Hebron protesters.
newsitem.headline: Undercover soldiers shock Hebron protesters.

text.p: Israeli soldiers posing as Palestinians stunned young Arab protesters on Thursday and arrested a handful of them at the start of stone-throwing in the West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said.
The undercover soldiers spoke Arabic, dressed like Palestinians in plain clothes and wore masks and keffiyeh headdresses while mingling with a crowd of about 50 youths.

When the group began hurling stones at uniformed troops and burning an Israeli flag, the undercover men began beating and pushing them, even dragging one along the ground, while making about six arrests, witnesses said.
The protests began near the Jewish enclave of Beit Hadassah on the Israeli-held side of the West Bank town which has been divided since January under a peace deal with the Palestinians.
After being surprised by the undercover soldiers, the protesters then retreated to the Palestinian-held side but continued to stone troops on the Israeli side.
The soldiers responded by firing rubber bullets while Israeli snipers armed with live ammunition deployed on rooftops for a second day.
Troops on Wednesday wounded 37 youths who launched protests against the pasting of posters on Palestinian shops on Saturday desecrating Islam's Prophet Mohammad and the holy Koran.

Israeli police are holding a 25-year-old Jewish woman suspected of gluing the posters -- which depicted Prophet Mohammad as a pig -- to some 20 Hebron storefronts. Israeli leaders repeatedly condemned the posters.
Soldiers shot dead an Arab teenager in a clash in Gaza.
Israel warned the Palestinian Authority to quell the violence or risk a stronger military response.
Israeli troops have clashed with Palestinians routinely since Israel began work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last March, plunging peacemaking into crisis.
